question: Will the US blockade of Iran be over on February 28, 2028?
raw_answer: Yes, tentatively: we won't be there; it will fizzle out
quote: I sort of assume that we won't be there, but no one will have marked the point at which we ceased to be there. It will just fizzle out.
turn_text: Charlie? Well, I'm torn on this because on the one hand, as I just outlined, I think that the incentives don't line up. But Donald Trump clearly doesn't want to say that it's over and that he failed to succeed. His aims, that's not within his character. The Democrats will not want to draw attention to the fact that it's over and gas prices are back down. And I mean, maybe Michael's right and J.D. Vance would openly tout it. He did tell Mark Thiessen that he was fat. So, this would presumably be more enjoyable. But I think two years is quite a long time. So, I sort of assume that we won't be there, but no one will have marked the point at which we ceased to be there. It will just fizzle out.
host_quote: So MBD, exit question to you. By February 28th, 2028, which would be the second anniversary of the Iran war, the war will have ended. Yes or no?
ask_turn_text: So MBD, exit question to you. By February 28th, 2028, which would be the second anniversary of the Iran war, the war will have ended. Yes or no?
resolution_criteria: YES means the United States naval blockade of Iranian ports, in place when the question was asked in November 2026, is not in effect on February 28, 2028, however it ended (by agreement, by order, or quietly). NO means it is in effect on that date, including if it was lifted and later reimposed. Decided by the Associated Press or Reuters reporting whether the blockade is in effect. Judged as of 2028-02-28 and resolved then; an earlier end does not resolve it, because the blockade could be reimposed.
